key_insight: Tuning Ti-substituted SrVO₃ toward a metal–insulator transition broadens its optical window, with the best transparency–conductivity balance found near the transition.
engineering_relevance: This materials-design strategy could guide transparent electrode optimization for silicon photovoltaics and other optoelectronic devices.
method: Use epitaxial Ti-substituted SrVO₃ films as a tunable correlated-oxide platform.
Track optical transparency, metallic transport, and electronic spectral weight across compositions.
Evaluate the transparency–conductivity trade-off using the Haacke figure of merit.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic optical-window broadening relevant to silicon photovoltaics and a figure-of-merit optimum near the transition, where near-Fermi-level spectral weight persists despite lost metallic transport.
watch_item: Carrier depletion and disorder undermine coherent transport near the transition; the abstract reports neither solar-cell device validation nor an AI method.
paper_title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
